I have read this and I understand it.

It reads a FreeStyle Libre 2 sensor of the European type and shows the glucose value. You scan the sensor with the phone (NFC). If you want, the sensor also sends a value each minute over Bluetooth ("Live values").

A scan only reads. It never changes the sensor. Only when you switch on live values, the app tells the sensor to send its values to this app. A new sensor must be started with the FreeStyle LibreLink app or the Libre 2 reader.

The app also looks at your values and says what stands out ("Analysis"), and it makes a report of a day with graphs as a PDF file ("Report"). It counts by fixed rules, on this phone. There is no AI inside the app; if you want, it asks an AI service over the internet.

The app uses the internet only for three things, and only after you have set them up: values from LibreLinkUp, questions to an AI service, and the online copy of your values. Without them your values stay on this phone; they leave it only when you send a file or a text yourself.
